note: NECO English round 6 (R49 top-up): synonyms commence, lucrative, dormant; antonyms agile, gregarious, abolish; idioms spill the beans, make hay while the sun shone, beat about the bush, took to his heels, break the ice; collocations heavy rain, make progress; word meaning novice, veteran; tenses present perfect continuous, past perfect continuous; preposition insists on; determiner fewer; passive transformation; orals vowel pain/reign, stress CONGRATULATIONS, DEMOCRACY, rhyme weight/freight, homophone sun/son. Scanned against the whole English pool (JAMB, WAEC and NECO stems).

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The new manager decided to COMMENCE trading on the first of the month. A word closest in meaning to COMMENCE is
questions.explanation: To commence is simply to begin.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Transport business between the two markets proved highly LUCRATIVE for the young trader. LUCRATIVE means
questions.explanation: Money comes home from a lucrative trade.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The seeds lie DORMANT in the dry soil until the rains return. DORMANT means
questions.explanation: Sleeping, but alive and waiting.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The AGILE athlete leaped over the hurdles with ease. A word opposite in meaning to AGILE is
questions.explanation: Where the agile leaps, the clumsy stumbles.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Chike is a GREGARIOUS young man who never eats lunch alone. A word opposite in meaning to GREGARIOUS is
questions.explanation: The sociable seek company; his opposite shuns it.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The new government decided to ABOLISH the old levy. A word opposite in meaning to ABOLISH is
questions.explanation: What is abolished is wiped away; its opposite is set up.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The little boy could not keep the secret; he SPILLED THE BEANS before the party. This means that he
questions.explanation: The beans of the matter poured out of his mouth.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Ada decided to MAKE HAY WHILE THE SUN SHONE by selling her yams while prices were high. This means that she
questions.explanation: Dry the grass while the weather agrees.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The candidate BEAT ABOUT THE BUSH for ten minutes before admitting that he had failed. This means that he
questions.explanation: He circled the matter without touching it.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: When the robbers were spotted, the thief TOOK TO HIS HEELS. This means that he
questions.explanation: The heels did the talking.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The chairman told a funny story at the start of the meeting to BREAK THE ICE. This means that he
questions.explanation: The first smile melts the frozen room.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The farmers were happy because the rainy season brought ____ rain that filled their wells.
questions.explanation: English rain is heavy, never strong.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: After months of steady practice, the choir began to ____ progress in their singing.
questions.explanation: Progress is made, not done.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Being a NOVICE on the job, Uche asked his senior colleagues to show him the way. A NOVICE is
questions.explanation: New to the work, still learning the ropes.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The VETERAN teacher could calm the noisiest class with a single look. A VETERAN is
questions.explanation: Long years on the job have taught her every trick.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The pupils ____ for the inter-house sports since six o'clock this morning, and the races have not begun.
questions.explanation: It started at six and continues now.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: By the time the help finally arrived, the farmers ____ in the sun for three hours.
questions.explanation: Three hours passed before the help came.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The workers' union insists ____ a pay rise before the unions call off the strike.
questions.explanation: To insist takes 'on', never 'for'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: There were ____ students at the morning assembly than the principal expected.
questions.explanation: Students can be counted; so 'fewer' is the word.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The play 'The Lion and the Jewel' ____ by Wole Soyinka.
questions.explanation: The play receives the writing; it does not do it.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: The 'ai' in 'pain' carries exactly the same vowel sound as the letters 'ei' in one of these words. Which one?
questions.explanation: Rain, reign and pain share one sound.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: In the word CONGRATULATIONS, the primary stress falls on the
questions.explanation: The voice lifts on the second beat: con-GRAT-u-la-tions.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: In the word DEMOCRACY, the primary stress falls on the
questions.explanation: de-MOC-ra-cy — the voice rises on the second beat.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: One of these words ends with exactly the same sounds as 'weight', so that the two make a perfect rhyme. It is
questions.explanation: Weight and freight ride in the same sounding wagon.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: When spoken aloud, 'sun' sounds exactly like one other word in English, though their spellings differ. That word is
questions.explanation: The star and the child answer to one sound.
